newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.6 pct in Jan - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.6 pct in Jan - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.6 percent in the first week of fiscal January versus December according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 6.2 percent compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 6.2 percent in the week ended January 11 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

The increase in retail sales was in line with the recent pace of business, although a number of department stores came below plan, partly due to adverse winter weather in the Pacific Northwest and Midwest, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
However, Eilenberg noted that some stores were comparing favorable sales against the big blizzard of 1996, which helped to balance some of the comparisons.
"The Pacific Northwest has been severly hurt (by storms) so, in some cases, it is a balance," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"But a year ago, the whole Northeast was closed down," he said.
In general, the pace of retail was moderately better than analysts had anticipated, Eilenberg said, but he cautioned that the level of business was "quite low."
Additionally, Eilenberg said some retailers have the chore of reducing an excess supply of goods left over from the holiday season.
"There are cases where stores have to clear their stocks, and perhaps they had too much left over (from the holiday) ... So they've got to promote even more," he said.
